Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — initial workload and ask

Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to move towards a Dedicated contract for production inference. We attached a summarized workload profile (queries per minute by model, context lengths, and 95th pct latency targets). High level:\n- Mixed usage: 60% embedding/semantic search (short contexts), 40% multimodal + long-form generation (avg context ~6k tokens).\n- Peak: ~3.5k concurrent inference streams during business hours, burstable to ~6k for launches.\n- Latency SLOs: embeddings <= 80ms p95, generation p95 target <= 700ms for typical prompts, with some long-generation tails acceptable.\n
Primary ask: recommendation on GPU SKU mix (H100 vs A100 vs L4) for a 12-18 month commitment that balances cost and predictable latency, plus the ops constraints we should plan for (oversubscription, fallbacks, cache strategy). Can you loop in the ops/engineering folks to propose an initial fleet topology and a canary plan?

Appreciate any quick guidance — we need something to bring to procurement next week.

Best,
Samantha
VP Product, Orchid Labs

Samantha — thanks for the profile, this is exactly the kind of signal we need. Looping in Dev (infra/runtime), Marcus (capacity modeling) and Grace (CS/ops) to propose a concrete recommendation.

High-level my read: embeddings-heavy short-context work maps economically to L4s or quantized A100 instances depending on model size; long-form multimodal/generation work benefits from H100s for memory headroom and throughput on long context. A hybrid fleet with regionally co-located H100 for generation pages and L4/A100 pool for embeddings could give the best cost/latency balance.

Requests to internal team: please draft a "starter topology" (SKU counts, throughput assumptions, cache/batching defaults, fallback model variants) and an ops playbook for canary + burst handling. Also include what we can offer as a short-term burst-credit or reserve-burst plan for their launch.

Samantha — we'll aim to provide a concise recommendation and an ops-runbook draft within 48 hours.

Cheers,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — initial workload and ask

Team — I analyzed the attached CSV and ran a quick sim using Orchid's qps/ctx distribution. Notes and suggestion below.

Summary of constraints:\n- Long-form generation (avg 6k tokens, tails to 20k): memory pressure + KV cache makes H100 attractive for large model variants; H100 also wins on single-stream latency for long contexts when using fused kernels.\n- Embeddings (short context, high qps): L4 provides excellent cost-per-embedding for smaller models (<2B) and supports dense batching; for larger embedding models (>7B) an int8 A100 configuration gives better memory/perf tradeoff.\n- Mixed traffic: the main risk is queueing under sudden bursts if we place everything on shared A100 slots without aggressive pre-warming / slot reservations.\n
Concrete starter topology (US region):\n- H100 pool: 8x H100 nodes (reserved). Purpose: long-context generation model variants and multimodal inference. Assumption: average concurrent generation streams 600, each H100 supports ~80-100 concurrent long-context streams depending on prompt shape.\n- A100 pool (int8 quantized): 12x A100 nodes. Purpose: medium embeddings and mid-size generation fallbacks. Good middle-ground for models ~7B-13B.\n- L4 pool: 24x L4 nodes. Purpose: high-qps short-context embeddings + cheap reranking. L4s used as front-line for low-latency embedding requests with batching window 10-20ms.\n
Operational levers and justifications:\n- Prefix/KV caching for conversational flows — saves ~30-45% token compute for multi-turn generation; recommend enabling on H100 pool by default.\n- Autoscaling thresholds: keep H100 autoscaler conservative (scale step 1-2 nodes) with aggressive pre-warm cron before known launches; L4 autoscaler can be more aggressive with fast spin-up.\n- Fallbacks: when H100 pool saturates, route to quantized A100 variants with the same model family and a client-visible degraded latency SLAs; for embedding tails, degrade to smaller embedding model on L4 if exact vector quality not critical.\n- Buffering/burst credits: propose a short-term burst buffer (20% of reserved capacity) for the first 90 days to absorb launch variance. This can be represented as a temporary headroom billing construct in the deal.\n
Perf numbers (simulated):\n- Embedding 512-token batch (L4): p95 ~ 45-60ms at 64 qps per L4 slot.\n- Generation 6k context (H100): p95 ~ 420-650ms depending on response length & sampling.\n- Quantized A100 fallback: generation p95 ~ 600-900ms but at ~40% lower cost than H100 for the same token count.\n
Risks and mitigations:\n- Memory-heavy model versions => require larger H100 headroom; mitigation: pin older model variants to A100/L4 with explicit quality guards.\n- Burst unpredictability => mitigation: canary + staged rollout, 7-day warm window, and a 30-day flexible buffer in contract.\n
I attached a quick latency/topology matrix and a starter mutual action plan for procurement (ORCH-2027-09_mutual_action_plan.xlsx).

—Dev
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — commercial implications and recommended contractual flex

Quick commercial thoughts:\n- Pricing: given Dev's starter topology, we can build the SOW as a three-tier reserve: H100 reserved blocks, A100 reserved blocks, L4 reserved blocks. Offer a 10% price break if they commit 12 months upfront, plus the 90-day 20% burst buffer as one-off credit.\n- Contract language: include a clause for "temporary headroom" that converts to billed usage if sustained beyond 90 days. This protects us and keeps Orchid happy at launch.\n- SLA: for H100-backed generation routes we can commit to p95 latency target band with credits tiered by severity; for A100 fallback routes list as "best-effort" with explicit fallback notice in console and routing policy.\n
Operational asks from CS/Ops: Grace, can you draft the canary runbook (traffic split %, monitoring hooks, rollback thresholds)? Marcus, please give a quick heatmap of utilization by hour so we can price the autoscaling headroom conservatively.

I'll prepare a clean commercial summary for the procurement packet.

—Ben
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
